title: Bradesco and evolutionQ Begin Quantum Communication Tests to Assess New Data Protection Models
html:
Insider Brief

  • Brazil’s Bradesco has begun testing quantum communication with Canadian cybersecurity company evolutionQ to assess whether it can help secure the exchange of sensitive information.
  • In a simulated environment, the teams will measure how the software performs and assess whether it can protect messages as they move between network points while keeping them accessible in real time without disrupting bank operations.
  • The initiative grew out of Bradesco’s QSafe program, with initial proofs of concept expected in the coming months.

PRESS RELEASE — A pioneering initiative in Brazil’s financial sector seeks to study, in a controlled environment, the feasibility of the technology and its potential to strengthen the security of information exchange among companies, financial institutions and startups in the coming years.

São Paulo, September 2026 — Bradesco, through inovabra, has begun pioneering tests in quantum communication, a technology that uses the principles of quantum physics to create information networks and transform the way sensitive information is shared between organizations. The initiative is led by inovabra and Bradesco’s cybersecurity team, in partnership with Canadian cybersecurity company evolutionQ, and aims to study and experiment with solutions capable of anticipating digital security challenges in the coming years.

In this first, exploratory phase, the teams will assess technologies and architectures which can enable more secure communication channels and new protection models for critical data. The tests will be conducted in a simulated environment, through the installation of software provided by the partner, allowing the solution’s operation to be observed in a controlled manner before any practical application.

The experiment aims to generate data on the solution’s feasibility for the bank’s operating environment, with a focus on three main areas. The first involves analyzing how information is securely exchanged between different points on a network.

The second seeks to verify whether messages can be protected and accessed in real time without affecting operations. Finally, the third will measure the solution’s performance throughout the process. The initiative is an outgrowth of the QSafe (Quantum Safe) program, created three years ago to track the evolution of cryptography and quantum technologies, and their potential long-term impacts on digital security and the financial market.

“At inovabra, we continuously monitor, experiment with and evaluate new emerging technologies that could affect the digital security of our ecosystem,” says Jonatas Rossetti, R&D specialist at Bradesco. “Quantum communication is a topic at the frontier of innovation in digital security. Our goal is to understand how these technologies evolve, assess their applicability and prepare the ecosystem for the challenges that may arise in the coming years,” he concludes.

Today, the exchange of information in the digital environment is protected by cryptographic systems widely used in the market. The industry’s concern is that advanced quantum computers could, in the future, overcome some of these security barriers, creating challenges for data protection.

The urgency of this movement is also due to the rapid advance of AI tools, which create new ways of breaking into systems, combined with the approaching era of quantum computers, which are capable of challenging the traditional encryption standards used around the world today.

“Quantum computing and AI are rapidly transforming the risk landscape. Financial institutions need a cryptographic infrastructure that can draw on additional sources of trust and adapt quickly, without interrupting operations. We are proud to work alongside inovabra to strengthen the cryptographic resilience of Brazil’s financial ecosystem,” says Michele Mosca, CEO and co-founder of evolutionQ.

The expectation is that the first proofs of concept and quantum communication architecture tests will be carried out in the coming months, serving as a basis for new research, development and experimentation initiatives at inovabra over the coming years.
